component-o.description-s: Energizer CR2032 lithium / manganese-dioxide coin cell, 3.0 V nominal, 235 mAh typical (to 2.0 V at 15 kohm), 20.0 x 3.2 mm, bulk

non-technical-o.stock-note-s: DigiKey N189-ND (CR2032VP), 181997 in stock, MOQ 200 (pcbparts digikey_get_part 2026-10-21)

source-o.table-s: Nominal Voltage 3.0 V; Typical Capacity 235 mAh (to 2.0 volts, rated at 15K ohms at 21 C); Max Rev Charge 1 uA; Operating Temp -30..60 C

source-o.figure-s: Pulse Discharge Characteristics: IR, ohms (right axis) vs capacity, 400 ohm 2 s pulses x12/day at 21 C
source-o.derived-s: read from the figure's vector curve with procurement pdf-graph --at 0,50,100,150,200 (fresh cell 9.5 ohm); a typical curve, not a guaranteed value

source-o.table-s: Typical Drains: Bkgnd Drain continuous 15K ohms 0.19 mA @2.9V; Pulse Drain 400 ohms ~6.8 mA @2.7V, 2 s x 12/day

not_stated-o.discharge-max-ma-i: Energizer states no maximum continuous or pulse current, only the typical test drains (0.19 mA continuous, ~6.8 mA pulse). For comparison Renata CR2032 MFR (Rev 07/2021) states Max. Cont. Discharge Current 3.0 mA (avg current for 70 % capacity to 2.0 V) -- a different maker's cell; Panasonic CR2032 states only 'continuous drain 0.2 mA'
not_stated-o.max_currents-ao: left out: no rated maximum current
not_stated-o.internal_resistance: no tabulated value; 9.5 ohm is the fresh-cell point of the datasheet's IR curve
